title: PowerPoint presentations (.pptx)
summary: Each slide is a page, drawn as an image.

items.text: Slides as pages: --page N (from 1), --all-pages, and --dpi.

Embedding: <image href="deck.pptx#slide=3" .../> in an SVG file draws slide 3 (#page=3 means the same; slide 1 without the fragment); a slide that does not exist is image-page-out-of-range. See 'canvasnet help svg'. On the command line the same fragment on the input chooses the slide: canvasnet render "deck.pptx#slide=3" -o s3.png (it overrides --page).
The shape tree including nested groups; preset and custom geometry with solid, linear-gradient, and covered pattern fills, and outlines.
Connectors (straight, elbow, and curved) with arrowheads.
Raster pictures (BMP, PNG, TIFF, JPEG, GIF, with srcRect cropping) and pictures that only carry an SVG.
Tables and embedded charts.
Text with placeholder, layout, master, and theme inheritance, wrapping, alignment, vertical anchoring, autofit, bullets, and numbering.
Slide, layout, and master backgrounds.
EMF and WMF pictures: they are skipped and reported (see diagnostics); --strict turns the report into an error. Those on a layout or master are skipped silently.

These always fail the page with unsupported-feature, with or without --strict: radial and path gradients (pptx-gradient-path), preset shapes or pattern fills the library lacks (pptx-pattern-fill), linked images that are not embedded (pptx-image-link), and picture formats it cannot decode (pptx-image-format).
A chart feature that cannot be drawn fails the page with unsupported-feature; the token names the feature.
A shape, picture, or graphic frame that has no position anywhere in its ancestry is skipped silently.
The slide to draw, counted from 1 (default 1).
Draw every slide; for a deck of more than one slide the output must contain {page} or be a directory.
Resolution in dots per inch (default 96, above 0 and at most {{maxDpi}}).
The color the slide is cleared to first (white by default); a declared slide background is painted over it.
Fail with unsupported-feature when an EMF or WMF picture would be skipped.
{source: pptx, severity: unsupported}: an EMF or WMF picture was skipped. It is the only skipped-picture report; with --strict it is an unsupported-feature error.
The other pptx-* identifiers appear in the message of an unsupported-feature error, not in diagnostics[].
Error code: see the list of failures above.
Error code: --page is beyond the last slide.
Fonts that are not embedded come from the machine, so text can differ between machines.
EMF and WMF pictures are not drawn (a known gap).
The result is a still picture of one slide.
